Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge to lead God's people. What would you ask God for?
God gave Solomon more than he asked. How has God been generous to you?
Solomon asked, "Who is able to build him a house, since heaven cannot contain him?" How do you approach the great God?
Hiram praised the God of Israel. How can others see God through your work?
Solomon began to build on the place where God had appeared. How does God's past faithfulness shape your future?
The temple was built with costly materials. How can you give God your best?
The temple furnishings were made with care. What does this show about honouring God?
The basins were for washing the offerings and the sea for the priests to wash in. Why does God call his people to be clean as they serve?
Solomon brought in the things David had dedicated. How can you finish well what others started faithfully?
When the singers praised, "For he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever," God's glory filled the house. How does praise welcome God's presence?
Solomon prayed that God would hear prayers made toward the temple. How does Jesus give us access to God?
Solomon prayed for those who sin and then turn back with all their heart. What does this show about God's mercy?
"Let your saints rejoice in your goodness." What goodness of God can you rejoice in?
Fire came down and the people said, "He is good, for his steadfast love endures forever." How do you respond to God's glory?
"If my people... humble themselves, and pray and seek my face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear." Which step do you need?
God warned what would happen if they turned away. Why does God warn us?
Solomon offered sacrifices according to the commandment. How can you worship God in his way?
Solomon organised worship as David had commanded. How can you continue faithful patterns of worship?
The queen of Sheba saw Solomon's wisdom and blessed the Lord. How can your life point others to God?
Solomon excelled all kings in riches and wisdom. What does Solomon's later life teach about riches?
Rehoboam ignored the wise counsel of the elders. Whose advice do you seek?
This turn of affairs was brought about by God. How does God work even through our mistakes?
God said, "You shall not fight against your relatives." What conflicts might God want you to step back from?
Priests and Levites left their land to seek the Lord in Jerusalem. What would you leave behind to seek God?
Rehoboam abandoned God's law when he was strong. How does success tempt us?
When they humbled themselves, God gave some deliverance. What does humility do?
Rehoboam did evil because he did not set his heart to seek the Lord. How can you set your heart on God?
Abijah said, "God is with us at our head." What does it mean that God leads you?
They cried to the Lord and he gave the victory, because they relied on him. How do you rely on God?
Asa commanded Judah to seek the Lord. What does seeking God look like for you?
Asa prayed, "Help us, O Lord our God, for we rely on you." Where do you need to pray this?
"The Lord is with you while you are with him. If you seek him, he will be found by you." How does this encourage you?
"Take courage! Do not let your hands be weak, for your work shall be rewarded." What work do you need encouragement in?
They sought God with their whole desire and he was found by them. What would seeking God with your whole desire look like?
"The eyes of the Lord run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to give strong support to those whose heart is blameless." How does this speak to you?
Asa did not seek the Lord in his illness. How can you seek God in every situation?
Jehoshaphat sought God and his heart was courageous in the ways of the Lord. What does a courageous heart look like?
Leaders taught the book of the law throughout Judah. How can you help others know God's word?
Jehoshaphat said, "Inquire first for the word of the Lord." Why ask God first?
Micaiah said, "What my God says, that I will speak." How can you speak truth with courage?
"Consider what you do... there is no injustice with the Lord." How can you act with fairness?
"Thus you shall do in the fear of the Lord, in faithfulness, and with your whole heart." Which do you need most?
Jehoshaphat was afraid and set his face to seek the Lord. What do you do with your fear?
"We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you." Where do you need to pray this?
"The battle is not yours but God's." What battle can you hand to God?
They sang praise as they went out, and God gave victory. How can praise help in hard times?
God did not destroy Judah because of his covenant with David. How does God's faithfulness hold when people fail?
Elijah wrote a warning to Jehoram. How does God warn us?
Ahaziah's mother counselled him to do wickedly. How do the voices around us shape us?
Jehoshabeath hid Joash and saved the royal line. How does God protect his promises?
Jehoiada took courage and acted. When might God be calling you to courageous action?
The people made a covenant to be the Lord's people, and the city was quiet. What does belonging to God bring?
Joash did right all the days of Jehoiada. How does godly influence shape a life?
The people gave gladly to restore the temple. What does joyful giving look like?
After Jehoiada died, Joash turned away. How can you build a faith that is your own?
Amaziah did right, but not with a whole heart. What does a whole heart look like?
The man of God said, "The Lord is able to give you much more than this." What might you need to let go of, trusting God?
Amaziah worshipped the gods he had defeated. Why do we turn to what cannot save us?
As long as Uzziah sought the Lord, God made him prosper. How do you keep seeking God when things go well?
When Uzziah was strong, he grew proud. How does pride creep in after success?
Jotham did what was right. What does faithful living look like in ordinary days?
Jotham became mighty because he ordered his ways before the Lord. How can you order your ways before God?
Ahaz did not do what was right. How can one leader's sin affect many?
The prophet Oded urged mercy, and the captives were clothed, fed and returned. How can you show mercy?
In his distress Ahaz became more faithless. How do you respond to God in distress?
Hezekiah opened the doors of the temple and called the priests to consecrate themselves. What doors in your life need opening to God?
They sang praises with gladness and bowed down and worshipped. What brings gladness in worship?
Hezekiah rejoiced because God had provided for the people. What has God provided for you?
"Return to the Lord... he is gracious and merciful and will not turn away his face from you." Where do you need to return?
Hezekiah prayed, "May the good Lord pardon everyone who sets his heart to seek God." What does this show about God's grace?
There was great joy and their prayer came to heaven. What brings joy in God's presence?
The people gave so generously there was plenty left over. What does abundant generosity look like?
Hezekiah did what was good, right and faithful, seeking God with all his heart. What does wholehearted work look like?
Hezekiah said, "With him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the Lord our God." Where do you need to remember this?
Hezekiah and Isaiah prayed and God saved them. How does prayer change things?
Hezekiah's heart became proud, but he humbled himself. How do you respond when you see pride in yourself?
Manasseh did terrible evil. How far can a person fall?
In distress Manasseh humbled himself greatly, and God heard him. What does this show about God's mercy?
Manasseh removed the idols he had set up. What does real repentance look like?
While still young, Josiah began to seek the God of David. How can young people seek God?
When Josiah heard the law, he tore his clothes. How do you respond to God's word?
Because Josiah's heart was tender and he humbled himself, God heard. What does a tender heart look like?
Josiah made a covenant to walk after the Lord with all his heart. What commitment could you make?
Josiah kept the Passover carefully. How do you remember God's rescue?
No Passover like it had been kept since Samuel. What would wholehearted worship look like for you?
Josiah did not listen to God's warning and died in battle. How can we miss God's voice?
God sent messengers persistently "because he had compassion on his people." What does this show about God?
Jerusalem fell and the land rested. What does this show about God's word coming true?
God stirred up Cyrus to let the people return. How does God work through unexpected people?
